title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #15

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the job of the ropes on a drum? (1 mark)
   A. To decorate the beater
   B. To hold the skin tight
   C. To make the shell heavy
   D. To make the drum float

2. How can you make the brightest part of a charcoal drawing? (1 mark)
   A. Leave the paper white or lift charcoal with a clean eraser
   B. Colour it black
   C. Press very hard
   D. Smudge with a wet cloth

3. What should you do after passing the ball? (1 mark)
   A. Walk off the court
   B. Sit down
   C. Close your eyes
   D. Move into space to receive it again

4. Which player mainly tries to stop the shooter? (1 mark)
   A. C
   B. GK
   C. GS
   D. WA

5. In a double-handed catch, where should your eyes be? (1 mark)
   A. On the ball until it is in your hands
   B. On the ground
   C. On the crowd
   D. On the next player

6. The game restarts after each goal with (1 mark)
   A. a centre pass
   B. a jump ball
   C. a throw-in from the side
   D. a penalty kick

7. Why should you take turns to talk about each other's work? (1 mark)
   A. It is fair and respectful
   B. So no one speaks
   C. To waste time
   D. To make others sad

8. A darker tone of a colour is called a (1 mark)
   A. frame
   B. secondary
   C. shade
   D. tint

9. A flat brush is best for (1 mark)
   A. tiny details only
   B. wide areas
   C. cutting paper
   D. writing with ink

10. What is the theme of the montage in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Ball games
   B. Food
   C. Weather
   D. Wild animals

11. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. Two quavers equal one crotchet
   B. A crotchet is shorter than a quaver
   C. A rest is longer than a note
   D. One quaver equals two crotchets

12. The steady pulse in a piece of music is called the (1 mark)
   A. lyric
   B. echo
   C. beat
   D. melody

13. The French rhythm name for a crotchet is (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. sh
   C. te-te
   D. ta-te

14. Which is a quality of a good rhythmic pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Variation of note values
   B. Ending on a rest always
   C. Only one kind of note
   D. No beat

15. The recorder notes G, A and B match the sol-fa syllables (1 mark)
   A. d, r and m
   B. m, d and r
   C. r, m and d
   D. m, r and d

16. How do you make a coil? (1 mark)
   A. Bake it
   B. Cut it flat
   C. Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   D. Beat it with a stick

17. Compared with the medium start, the elongated start has the back knee (1 mark)
   A. on the line
   B. further back
   C. in the air
   D. further forward

18. The middle stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. green
   C. red
   D. black

19. In a crab balance, what is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Hips sagging near the mat
   B. Head in line
   C. Hips lifted
   D. Straight arms

20. A roll in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   C. a run
   D. a still position

21. Why do we stand up slowly after a side roll? (1 mark)
   A. To look tall
   B. To avoid feeling dizzy
   C. To make noise
   D. To win a prize

22. Why should you sing folk songs from other communities with respect? (1 mark)
   A. They are funny
   B. They are unimportant
   C. They must be changed
   D. They are part of our shared culture

23. Singing in unison means (1 mark)
   A. everyone sings the same notes at the same time
   B. everyone sings different tunes
   C. nobody sings
   D. only one sings

24. What is the danger of pointing a camera directly at the sun? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the picture sharper
   B. It makes the sun cooler
   C. It saves the battery
   D. It can hurt your eyes and spoil the picture

25. Where must you never take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. In the classroom with permission
   B. In private places such as toilets
   C. In the playground with permission
   D. At the school gate

26. If the bright sun is behind your subject, the subject will (1 mark)
   A. turn blue
   B. be dark with the face in shadow
   C. be lit clearly
   D. disappear

27. The word photography comes from words meaning (1 mark)
   A. drawing with paint
   B. drawing with sound
   C. drawing with light
   D. writing with ink

28. To keep the camera steady you should (1 mark)
   A. hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   B. shake it
   C. hold it at arm's length with one finger
   D. throw it

29. Why delete poor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. So memory is not filled up
   B. To make the screen dark
   C. To break the camera
   D. To cool it

30. Where is the thumb hole? (1 mark)
   A. At the back
   B. On the mouthpiece
   C. Under the foot
   D. On the bell

31. When you make a mistake while playing in a group, you should (1 mark)
   A. carry on with the beat
   B. stop the whole group
   C. shout
   D. throw your recorder

32. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3 covered? (1 mark)
   A. G
   B. A
   C. F
   D. B

33. What should you do before playing to prevent spreading germs? (1 mark)
   A. Eat sweets
   B. Chew gum
   C. Share the recorder
   D. Wash your hands

34. Swimming is important because (1 mark)
   A. it needs no rules
   B. it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   C. it replaces school
   D. it makes water disappear

35. After entering, you should (1 mark)
   A. stay at the edge
   B. move away from the edge so the next person can enter
   C. sit at the top
   D. pull others in

36. In the sit-and-slide entry, you should turn (1 mark)
   A. to face the wall and hold the edge
   B. upside down
   C. to the deep end
   D. away from the wall

37. Which is part of pool hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Not showering
   B. Eating in the pool
   C. Wearing dirty clothes
   D. Not passing urine or spitting in the pool

38. Two stars and a wish means (1 mark)
   A. two mistakes and a prize
   B. two songs and a wish
   C. two good comments and one suggestion
   D. two lines and a circle

39. To appreciate a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. notice, understand and value it
   B. hide it
   C. copy it exactly
   D. destroy it

40. What should be written on the portfolio label? (1 mark)
   A. Your name, class and title
   B. The price
   C. Nothing
   D. A secret

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give one example of a melodic percussion instrument and one non-melodic percussion instrument. (2 marks)

42. State how many finger holes a descant recorder has in front and where the thumb hole is. (2 marks)

43. Give four safety rules for sprint races. (4 marks)

44. Explain how to prepare and perform a folk song with your class. (5 marks)

45. Describe the steps of taking a photograph with a digital device. (5 marks)

46. Why is it important to appreciate the works of people from different cultures? (3 marks)

47. Compose a four-beat rhythmic pattern using a crotchet, a pair of quavers and a rest, and write it in rhythm names. (4 marks)

48. Why do we get up slowly after a side roll? (3 marks)

49. Why does a drum sound higher when its skin is tightened? (3 marks)

50. Write the rhythm names of a pattern of a crotchet, a crotchet rest, a pair of quavers and a crotchet. (3 marks)

51. Describe how to make a value scale strip of orange. (3 marks)

52. Explain how to tie an overhand knot. (3 marks)

53. Explain what a relay race is and how it teaches teamwork. (4 marks)

54. Name two parts of a drum. (2 marks)

55. Explain why a pair of quavers is the same length as one crotchet. (3 marks)

56. What is a sequence in gymnastics? Give an example. (3 marks)

57. Name three types of Kenyan folk songs and say when each is sung. (3 marks)

58. Why do we play water games in shallow water with the teacher? (3 marks)

59. What are indigenous games? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — To hold the skin tight
   Ropes or lacing keep the skin stretched tight.

2. A — Leave the paper white or lift charcoal with a clean eraser
   The brightest parts have little or no charcoal.

3. D — Move into space to receive it again
   Moving into open space keeps the game flowing.

4. B — GK
   The Goal Keeper guards the goal and defends against the shooter.

5. A — On the ball until it is in your hands
   Watching the ball helps you catch it.

6. A — a centre pass
   The game restarts with a centre pass, and the teams take turns.

7. A — It is fair and respectful
   Taking turns shows respect and love for others.

8. C — shade
   Adding black makes a shade.

9. B — wide areas
   Flat brushes cover wide areas quickly.

10. A — Ball games
   The montage is themed ball games.

11. A — Two quavers equal one crotchet
   1/2 + 1/2 = 1 beat.

12. C — beat
   The beat is the steady pulse we tap or clap along to.

13. A — taa
   Taa is the name for one long sound in one beat.

14. A — Variation of note values
   Good patterns vary the note values.

15. A — d, r and m
   If G is doh, then A is ray and B is me.

16. C — Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   Rolling back and forth makes a long even coil.

17. B — further back
   Elongated means longer, so the feet are further apart.

18. C — red
   Red is the middle stripe.

19. A — Hips sagging near the mat
   Hips should stay lifted to make the body level.

20. B — a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   A roll turns the body over along the mat.

21. B — To avoid feeling dizzy
   Getting up too fast can make you dizzy.

22. D — They are part of our shared culture
   Respect helps unity and cultural appreciation.

23. A — everyone sings the same notes at the same time
   Unison means the same notes together.

24. D — It can hurt your eyes and spoil the picture
   Looking at the sun harms the eyes.

25. B — In private places such as toilets
   Privacy must be respected.

26. B — be dark with the face in shadow
   The face is in shadow.

27. C — drawing with light
   Photography means drawing with light.

28. A — hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   A steady hold gives a sharp photograph.

29. A — So memory is not filled up
   Deleting saves space.

30. A — At the back
   The left thumb covers the hole at the back.

31. A — carry on with the beat
   Continue and rejoin.

32. A — G
   G adds the third hole.

33. D — Wash your hands
   Clean hands help hygiene.

34. B — it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   Swimming helps prevent drowning.

35. B — move away from the edge so the next person can enter
   Make space for others.

36. A — to face the wall and hold the edge
   You hold the edge as you lower yourself in.

37. D — Not passing urine or spitting in the pool
   Keeping the pool clean matters.

38. C — two good comments and one suggestion
   Give two positives and one idea to improve.

39. A — notice, understand and value it
   Appreciation is valuing with understanding.

40. A — Your name, class and title
   A label shows whose portfolio it is.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Melodic: xylophone. Non-melodic: shaker, kayamba or claves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Seven finger holes in front and the thumb hole is at the back.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Run in your own lane; check the track for stones; wear proper clothes; never push or trip; slow down gradually after the finish; warm up. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a song and say the community, type and message. Share roles among soloist, chorus and instrumentalists. Practise pitch, rhythm, tempo and dynamics. Add gestures and expressions. Perform with respect and take a bow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing the song, roles, practising, expression and performing respectfully.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Check the battery and memory and wipe the lens. Decide the subject. Check the light and centre of interest. Hold with two hands and keep elbows close. Frame the subject and press the button gently. Check the result and retake if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid stage.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: We learn about others, it builds respect and unity and it helps us value all cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example taa ta-te (rest) taa. Any four-beat pattern with all three parts and ending on a crotchet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four beats, 1 mark for using all three, 1 mark for correct names, 1 mark for ending on a long note.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Getting up fast can make you feel dizzy and you may fall. Slowly is safer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dizziness, 1 mark for falling, 1 mark for safety.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: A tighter skin vibrates faster. Faster vibration makes a higher sound. Ropes are used to tighten the skin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for faster vibration, 1 mark for higher sound, 1 mark for the ropes or tightening.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: taa (rest) ta-te taa
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part in order.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw a strip and divide it into five boxes. Mix orange with white for the two light boxes. Paint pure orange in the middle. Mix orange with black for the two dark boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the five boxes, 1 mark for light tones, 1 mark for dark tones.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a loop with the cord. Pass the end through the loop. Pull both ends to tighten.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: A relay is a race in which each runner in a team runs a short distance and passes a baton to the next runner. The team wins by working together and passing smoothly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for team running, 1 mark for the baton, 2 marks for teamwork explanation.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drumhead (skin) and shell (body). Rope and beater are also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quaver is half a beat. Half plus half makes one whole beat. A crotchet is one beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: A set of movements done in a fixed order. For example crab balance, lower to the mat, lie straight, side roll.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the correct example.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Work songs during work, funeral songs when someone dies, naming songs when a baby is named, initiation songs at initiation, marriage songs at weddings, worship songs at worship. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type with its occasion.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: To feel safe and in control, to learn to breathe and move with confidence and to avoid accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Traditional games that belong to a people and were passed on from long ago.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
